findings.title: filenamify output is not NFC-normalized when the replacement is non-NFC (not idempotent)
findings.property: filenamify(filenamify(x, o), o) equals filenamify(x, o); output is always NFC
findings.expected: Output normalized to NFC ('aéb' with U+00E9), so re-applying filenamify returns the same string
findings.actual: Returns 'ae\u0301b' (decomposed); filenamify of that returns 'a\u00E9b', a different string
findings.evidence: Source comment: 'Normalize to NFC first to stabilize byte representation and length calculations across platforms.' The input is NFC-normalized but the replacement is inserted afterwards without normalization, so the stated stabilization goal is not met.

error.message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

'aéb' !== 'aéb'

review.title: Output not NFC-normalized when a caller-supplied replacement is non-NFC
review.reason: filenamify only normalizes the input string to NFC (filenamify.js line 83). The `replacement` is a caller-chosen literal that is inserted verbatim, and nothing in the README, types or tests promises NFC output or idempotence for arbitrary replacements. The comment only says the input is normalized first, for stable length calculations. A non-NFC replacement is a deliberate choice by the caller, and the same applies to the replacement-based fallback paths. A maintainer would not treat this as a defect, and might at most call normalizing the replacement an optional nicety.
